noUnboundedLoops.note: Two loops in migrate(): sum amounts[] and redeposit per non-zero amount. Both bounded by the owner-supplied users[] length; owner is trusted (Law 3) and batches are paged off-chain via the staker's getStakersRange. No untrusted caller can reach either loop.

checkedArithmetic.note: solc 0.8.28; the only arithmetic is `total += amounts[i]` (checked). No unchecked, no assembly.

reentrancyUnguardedByDesign.reason: No nonReentrant, but onlyOwner and all external calls (oldStaker.batchMigrate, newStaker.depositFor) target immutable, owner-configured trusted StableStaker instances. forceApprove(total) is set fresh each call. No user-reachable reentrancy.

initializerProtected.note: Not upgradeable; constructor sets immutable oldStaker/newStaker and Ownable owner.

pausable.note: No pause mechanism; orchestration is owner-only and one-shot per batch.

notFlaggedDeferredToInteraction: Whether the amounts[] returned by oldStaker.batchMigrate truly satisfy Sigma amounts <= R (solvency) and equal-principal-equal-credit is a property of StableStaker (profiled there as INV-SS-5/6); the migrator trusts it as an axiom. Cross-contract verification -> interaction analysis.

Wiring correctness (migrator set as `migrator` on BOTH stakers; newStaker has token registered and is a phUSD minter) is a deployment/interaction concern; misconfiguration causes a safe revert, not a silent loss.

externalEntryPoints.note: thin owner-only forwarder; reverts on the staker if already migrating (idempotent-guarded). Call once per token before first migrate().

externalCalls: newStaker.depositFor(token, users[i], amounts[i]) per non-zero amount
externalEntryPoints.loop: sum amounts[] then redeposit per non-zero (bounded by users[] length)
externalEntryPoints.note: no-op (emits Migrated(token,0,0)) when total==0; approval(total) == Sigma deposits so no dangling allowance under standard ERC20

externalCalls.notes: Owner-configured StableStaker; migrator must be its `migrator`. batchMigrate pulls principal out and mints each user's phUSD, returns per-user credits and transfers their sum to this contract.
Owner-configured target StableStaker; migrator must be its `migrator`, must have token registered (addToken) and be a phUSD minter. depositFor pulls amounts[i] from this contract via transferFrom.

Standard ERC20 assumed. forceApprove(newStaker, total) is granted then fully consumed by the redeposit loop (total == Sigma amounts), so allowance returns to 0. Fee-on-transfer would break the approval==pull equality (known-issue exclusion).

localInvariants.statement: migrate forceApproves newStaker for exactly `total = Sigma amounts[i]`, then redeposits exactly amounts[i] per non-zero user, so the granted allowance is fully consumed and no dangling allowance remains (under standard ERC20).
localInvariants.evidence: L62-81: total summed from the same amounts[] array that drives the depositFor loop; forceApprove(total) at L73; Sigma depositFor pulls == total.

localInvariants.statement: The migrator holds the staked token only transiently within a single migrate() call: batchMigrate transfers `total` in, the redeposit loop sends `total` back out via newStaker.depositFor. Net token balance change per call is zero under standard ERC20.
localInvariants.evidence: batchMigrate sends Sigma amounts to msg.sender (the migrator); migrate redeposits the same Sigma amounts. No long-term custody, no per-user balance retained.

localInvariants.statement: A migrate() batch is all-or-nothing: any revert in batchMigrate, forceApprove, or a depositFor in the loop reverts the entire transaction, so partial/inconsistent migration state cannot persist.
localInvariants.evidence: No try/catch; single transaction. Already-self-migrated users surface as amounts[i]==0 and are skipped (no double-credit).

trustAssumptions: Owner is trusted and non-malicious (Law 3); both state-changing functions are onlyOwner.

oldStaker and newStaker are the genuine, correctly-wired StableStaker instances passed at construction (immutable). The migrator address must equal `migrator` on BOTH stakers, and newStaker must have the token registered and be an authorized phUSD minter; otherwise the relevant call reverts (safe-fail, no silent loss).
The token is a standard ERC20 (no fee-on-transfer); FoT would break the total==Sigma-deposits equality and could leave residual allowance/dust.
The per-user `amounts` returned by batchMigrate are taken as axiomatic (correctness proven in StableStaker INV-SS-5/6); the migrator does not re-derive credits.
